author: Elastic
attributes.description: Identifies an IAM policy change on a Google Cloud project, folder, or organization that grants a Vertex AI role (`roles/aiplatform.*`) to a principal. Vertex AI roles control who can invoke models, deploy endpoints, run agents, and read prompt and training data. An adversary who has gained IAM administration rights can grant a Vertex AI role to an identity they control to keep model access after the original foothold is removed, or to run LLMjacking workloads under the victim's billing. Google-managed service agent roles are excluded because Google grants them automatically when the API is enabled.
false_positives: Platform or ML engineering teams granting Vertex AI access to new users and service accounts. Confirm the grant against change records or the access request process.
Infrastructure-as-code pipelines that manage project IAM bindings. Add exceptions for the service accounts that run these pipelines.
attributes.name: GCP Vertex AI Role Granted to Principal
attributes.note:
## Triage and analysis

### Investigating GCP Vertex AI Role Granted to Principal

A Google Cloud IAM policy change added a binding for a Vertex AI role (`roles/aiplatform.*`). Roles such as
`roles/aiplatform.admin` and `roles/aiplatform.user` allow the member to call models, manage endpoints and agents, and
access prompt and training data in the project.

### Possible investigation steps

- Identify the caller that changed the policy from `client.user.email`, and review `source.ip` and
  `user_agent.original` for the change.
- Review `gcp.audit.service_data.policy_delta.binding_deltas` for the role and member that were added. Members outside
  the organization's domain, newly created service accounts, and `allUsers` or `allAuthenticatedUsers` are the most
  concerning.
- Check `gcp.audit.resource_name` to see whether the grant was made at the project, folder, or organization level.
  Grants above the project level reach every project underneath.
- Look for follow-on activity by the new member in Vertex AI audit logs, such as inference calls from new networks,
  endpoint deployment, or agent creation.
- Review other recent IAM changes by the same caller, especially service account key creation and grants of IAM admin
  roles.

### False positive analysis

- Approved access requests for ML and data science teams. Confirm with the request owner.
- IAM automation that reapplies bindings. Exclude those service accounts by email.

### Response and remediation

- If the grant is not authorized, remove the binding and review what the member accessed since the grant.
- Investigate how the caller obtained IAM administration rights, rotate its credentials, and review its other changes.
- Restrict `resourcemanager.projects.setIamPolicy` to a small set of administrators and consider an Organization Policy
  that limits allowed member domains.
attributes.query:
data_stream.dataset: "gcp.audit"
  and event.action: (
    "SetIamPolicy" or
    google.cloud.resourcemanager.v*.Folders.SetIamPolicy or
    google.cloud.resourcemanager.v*.Organizations.SetIamPolicy or
    google.cloud.resourcemanager.v*.Projects.SetIamPolicy
  )
  and not event.outcome: "failure"
  and gcp.audit.service_data.policy_delta.binding_deltas:{
    action: "ADD" and
    role: (roles/aiplatform.* and not (*ServiceAgent or *serviceAgent))
  }
attributes.setup:
## Setup

This rule requires Google Cloud Audit Logs ingested via the GCP integration (`gcp.audit` data stream). IAM policy
changes are Admin Activity audit logs and are always logged.
